title: Most commentators hear “visit the graves” as dying

points.label: Dying and burial
points.text: **Al-Ṭabarī** glosses it “until you reached the graves and were buried”; **Ibn Kathīr** calls this the sound sense. The rivalry lasts a lifetime. ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz drew more from the verb: a visitor must **go home**.

points.label: Counting the dead
points.text: **Muqātil and al-Kalbī** tie the verse to two Quraysh clans, Banū ʿAbd Manāf and Banū Sahm, who counted their living, then **went to the graveyards** to tally their dead. Here the visit is literal, a boast taken to its limit.

bottom_text: The classical commentaries lean to dying, but the story survives: al-Qurṭubī and the Jalālayn keep both. Occasion reports also vary; Qatāda names Jews boasting of numbers instead.
source_label: al-Ṭabarī, al-Baghawī, al-Qurṭubī, Ibn Kathīr on 102:2
